In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying statistical tools to analyze protein structures and to evaluate the accuracy and performance of protein structure prediction methods.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the order of the sequence-structure dependency in a protein chain is not a single value and it varies across the sequence.
the best method for protein structure prediction depends on the protein structure and the type of the prediction method.

a mixture of multivariate Gaussian distributions can be used to model the lag-distributions of dihedral angles with a reasonable number of mixture components (e.g. 3-5) and the order of the sequence-structure dependency can be captured by considering a maximum of lag 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bivariate lag-distribution of angles provides an efficient and accurate way for assessing the performance of angular-sampling based methods.
the bivariate lag-distribution of angles is informative and can be used as an assessment tool for different protein conformational methods.
a mixture of two components is a reasonable choice to model the distribution of the angles and the local dependency of the angles is captured by the lag 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bivariate lag-distribution of protein angles can be used to compare and evaluate model fits of the angular-sampling-based prediction methods.
there is no single best model for all the angles, and the choice of the model depends on the angles being studied.
the best distribution for modeling the protein angles should be the mixture of multivariate von Mises-Fisher distributions.
